questions.stem: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration in a cell?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration releases energy from glucose using oxygen, and the enzymes for this are held in the mitochondrion. Its inner membrane is folded into cristae, giving a large surface area for those enzymes, which is why energy-hungry cells such as muscle cells contain thousands of mitochondria.

distractorRationale.a: The nucleus stores DNA and controls the cell; it does not release energy
distractorRationale.c: Ribosomes assemble amino acids into proteins
distractorRationale.d: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins for export

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is found in a plant cell but not in an animal cell?
questions.explanation: Only plant cells have a rigid wall made of cellulose outside the cell membrane; it gives the cell its fixed shape and stops it bursting when it takes in water. The membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus are present in both plant and animal cells.

distractorRationale.a: Every living cell, plant or animal, is bounded by a cell membrane
distractorRationale.c: Cytoplasm fills both plant and animal cells
distractorRationale.d: Both plant and animal cells are eukaryotic and have a nucleus

questions.stem: The part of the cell that controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell is the
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is partially permeable: it allows small molecules such as water and oxygen through but blocks or actively selects larger ones. That selectivity is what makes it the gatekeeper of the cell.

distractorRationale.a: The cell wall is fully permeable — almost everything passes through it, so it cannot control entry
distractorRationale.c: The vacuole stores sap inside the cell; it does not border the outside
distractorRationale.d: The nucleolus inside the nucleus makes ribosomes

questions.stem: A cell examined under a microscope has a rigid rectangular outline, a large central space filling most of its middle, and green discs in the thin layer of cytoplasm. The cell is most likely from
questions.explanation: Three features point the same way: a rigid outline means a cellulose cell wall, a large central space is the permanent sap vacuole, and green discs are chloroplasts. Chloroplasts only develop where light reaches, so the cell comes from a green leaf rather than from a root.

distractorRationale.a: Liver cells are animal cells with no wall, no large vacuole and no chloroplasts
distractorRationale.c: Bacteria are far smaller, have no chloroplasts and no large sap vacuole
distractorRationale.d: Cheek cells are irregular animal cells without walls or chloroplasts

questions.stem: Which feature shows that a bacterium is a prokaryotic organism?

options.text: Its genetic material is not enclosed in a nuclear membrane

questions.explanation: The defining feature of a prokaryote is the absence of a true nucleus: the DNA is a single circular molecule lying free in the cytoplasm. Prokaryotes also lack mitochondria, chloroplasts and other membrane-bound organelles.

distractorRationale.b: Plant and fungal cells also have walls, so a wall does not indicate a prokaryote
distractorRationale.c: All cells contain cytoplasm
distractorRationale.d: Many eukaryotes, including yeast and Amoeba, also reproduce asexually

questions.stem: Cells of the pancreas secrete large quantities of digestive enzymes. Which two organelles would be unusually abundant in these cells?
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, so a secretory cell needs many ribosomes to synthesise them and many Golgi bodies to modify and package them into vesicles for export. Structure always follows function: an organelle is abundant where its job is in heavy demand.

distractorRationale.a: Chloroplasts occur only in green plant cells, not in the pancreas
distractorRationale.c: Lysosomes digest material inside the cell rather than exporting it
distractorRationale.d: Animal cells have neither cell walls nor plasmodesmata

questions.stem: Which organelle contains enzymes that digest worn-out organelles and bacteria taken into the cell?
questions.explanation: A lysosome is a small membrane-bound sac of hydrolytic enzymes. Keeping those enzymes inside a membrane protects the rest of the cell from being digested, and the sac fuses with material that must be broken down.

distractorRationale.c: Smooth ER synthesises lipids and steroids
distractorRationale.d: Mitochondria release energy; they do not digest organelles

questions.stem: The cell wall of a plant cell is partially permeable and therefore controls which substances enter the cell.
questions.explanation: False. The cellulose cell wall is fully permeable — water and dissolved substances pass through it freely, and its job is mechanical support. It is the cell membrane just inside it that is partially permeable and controls entry and exit.

questions.stem: A mature human red blood cell has no nucleus and no mitochondria. Which conclusion follows from this?

options.text: It cannot divide and it depends on anaerobic respiration for energy
It cannot change shape as it passes through capillaries

questions.explanation: Cell division is directed by the chromosomes in the nucleus, so a cell without a nucleus cannot divide; and without mitochondria it cannot carry out aerobic respiration, so it relies on glycolysis, an anaerobic pathway. Losing these organelles frees space for more haemoglobin.

distractorRationale.b: Oxygen is carried by haemoglobin in the cytoplasm, which the cell retains
distractorRationale.c: It develops from a nucleated eukaryotic stem cell; losing a nucleus does not make a cell prokaryotic
distractorRationale.d: Red blood cells are highly flexible precisely because they lack a rigid nucleus

questions.stem: State the cell theory and explain, with two examples, how the number of a particular organelle in a cell can be related to the work that cell does.
markingGuide: Cell theory: all living things are made of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells come from pre-existing cells (3 marks, 1 each)
Example 1: muscle or sperm cells contain many mitochondria because contraction or swimming needs a large, continuous supply of energy from aerobic respiration (2 marks)
Example 2: pancreatic or salivary gland cells contain many ribosomes and Golgi bodies because they synthesise and export large amounts of enzyme protein (2 marks)
General principle stated: the abundance of an organelle reflects the metabolic demand placed on its function, so structure follows function (1 mark)
questions.explanation: A full answer gives the three statements of the cell theory and then links organelle abundance to demand: mitochondria are numerous where energy use is high, while ribosomes and Golgi bodies are numerous where protein is exported. The underlying principle is that structure follows function.

questions.stem: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis in a cell?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis in the cell. They translate messenger RNA into polypeptide chains, which then fold into functional proteins.

distractorRationale.b: Lysosomes are involved in digestion and waste removal, not protein synthesis.
distractorRationale.c: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins but does not synthesize them.
distractorRationale.d: The endoplasmic reticulum assists in the synthesis and transport of proteins but does not synthesize them directly.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the cell membrane?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane regulates the transport of materials in and out of the cell, maintaining homeostasis. It is selectively permeable, allowing certain substances to pass while blocking others.

distractorRationale.a: Energy production occurs in the mitochondria, not the cell membrane.
distractorRationale.c: Genetic material is stored in the nucleus, not the cell membrane.
distractorRationale.d: Protein synthesis occurs mainly on ribosomes, not in the cell membrane.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells possess a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane, along with various membrane-bound organelles. This distinguishes them from prokaryotic cells, which lack a nucleus.

distractorRationale.a: Eukaryotic cells have membrane-bound organelles.
distractorRationale.c: Eukaryotic cells can be unicellular or multicellular.
distractorRationale.d: Eukaryotic cells have linear DNA, while prokaryotic cells have circular DNA.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are known as the powerhouse of the cell because they produce ATP through the process of cellular respiration, providing energy for cellular activities.

distractorRationale.a: The nucleus stores genetic information, but it does not produce energy.
distractorRationale.c: Chloroplasts are involved in photosynthesis, not energy production in the form of ATP.
distractorRationale.d: Ribosomes are involved in protein synthesis, not energy production.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: What distinguishes plant cells from animal cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are the organelles responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells, which is a key feature that distinguishes them from animal cells, which do not have chloroplasts.

distractorRationale.a: Both plant and animal cells have cell membranes.
distractorRationale.c: Ribosomes are present in both plant and animal cells.
distractorRationale.d: Mitochondria are present in both plant and animal cells.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: Which of the following organelles is responsible for packaging and distributing proteins?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus is responsible for modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins for secretion or delivery to other organelles. It plays a critical role in the cell's transport system.

distractorRationale.a: Lysosomes are involved in digestion and waste processing.
distractorRationale.c: Rough endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes proteins but does not package them.
distractorRationale.d: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification, not protein packaging.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: What is the function of the vacuole in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Vacuoles in plant cells are primarily responsible for the storage of substances such as nutrients, waste products, and water. They help maintain turgor pressure, which is essential for plant structure.

distractorRationale.a: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, not vacuoles.
distractorRationale.c: Protein synthesis occurs on ribosomes, not in vacuoles.
distractorRationale.d: Cell division is regulated by the nucleus, not the vacuole.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about prokaryotic cells is true?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles and do not have a true nucleus. Their genetic material is located in a nucleoid region, and they can reproduce asexually through binary fission.

distractorRationale.a: Prokaryotic cells do not have a true nucleus; they have a nucleoid.
distractorRationale.b: Prokaryotic cells can be unicellular or multicellular, though most are unicellular.
distractorRationale.d: Prokaryotic cells primarily reproduce asexually, although some can exchange genetic material through horizontal gene transfer.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: Which organelle is involved in detoxifying harmful substances in the cell?
questions.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is involved in the detoxification of harmful substances and the metabolism of carbohydrates and lipids. It lacks ribosomes, which distinguishes it from the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

distractorRationale.a: Lysosomes are involved in digestion, not detoxification.
distractorRationale.c: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins but does not detoxify substances.
distractorRationale.d: Mitochondria are primarily responsible for energy production, not detoxification.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: What is the role of ribosomes in a cell?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the cellular machinery that synthesizes proteins by translating messenger RNA into amino acid sequences. They can be found free in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

distractorRationale.a: Energy production occurs in mitochondria, not ribosomes.
distractorRationale.b: Lipid synthesis occurs in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, not ribosomes.
distractorRationale.d: Cell division involves various cellular processes, but ribosomes specifically synthesize proteins.

questions.stem: Which of the following organelles is involved in the synthesis of ATP?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are known as the powerhouse of the cell because they are responsible for synthesizing ATP through cellular respiration, which provides energy for the cell's activities.

distractorRationale.a: Chloroplasts are involved in photosynthesis, not ATP synthesis.
distractorRationale.b: The nucleus contains genetic material but is not involved in ATP synthesis.
distractorRationale.d: Ribosomes are involved in protein synthesis, not ATP synthesis.

questions.stem: Which part of the cell is responsible for controlling the activities of the cell?
questions.explanation: The nucleus is known as the control center of the cell because it contains the genetic material (DNA) that regulates cell functions. It directs the synthesis of proteins and controls cell division.

distractorRationale.a: The cell membrane regulates what enters and exits the cell but does not control cell activities.
distractorRationale.c: The cytoplasm is the site where many cellular processes occur but does not control the cell.
distractorRationale.d: Ribosomes are involved in protein synthesis but do not control the cell.

questions.stem: Which of the following organelles is responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are the organelles in plant cells that capture light energy and convert it into chemical energy through the process of photosynthesis. This process produces glucose and oxygen.

distractorRationale.b: Mitochondria are involved in cellular respiration, not photosynthesis.
distractorRationale.c: The endoplasmic reticulum is involved in protein and lipid synthesis, not photosynthesis.
distractorRationale.d: The Golgi apparatus is responsible for modifying and packaging proteins, not for photosynthesis.

questions.stem: What is one main difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?

options.text: Prokaryotic cells have a nucleus, while eukaryotic cells do not.
Eukaryotic cells are generally smaller than prokaryotic cells.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles, while eukaryotic cells have them.
Eukaryotic cells reproduce asexually, while prokaryotic cells reproduce sexually.

questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells are characterized by the absence of membrane-bound organelles and a true nucleus, while eukaryotic cells have these structures. This distinction is fundamental in cell biology.

distractorRationale.a: Actually, prokaryotic cells do not have a nucleus.
distractorRationale.b: Eukaryotic cells are generally larger than prokaryotic cells.
distractorRationale.d: Both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells can reproduce asexually.

questions.stem: Which organelle is primarily involved in lipid synthesis?
questions.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is involved in the synthesis of lipids and detoxification of drugs and poisons. Unlike the rough ER, it does not have ribosomes attached.

distractorRationale.a: Ribosomes are primarily involved in protein synthesis.
distractorRationale.c: Lysosomes contain enzymes for digestion and waste removal, not lipid synthesis.
distractorRationale.d: The nucleus contains genetic material but is not directly involved in lipid synthesis.

questions.stem: What is the function of the Golgi apparatus?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles. It is essential for the processing of macromolecules.

distractorRationale.a: Energy production occurs in mitochondria, not the Golgi apparatus.
distractorRationale.c: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, not the Golgi apparatus.
distractorRationale.d: Cell division is not a function of the Golgi apparatus.

options.text: They have a rigid cell wall.

questions.explanation: Plant cells are characterized by having a rigid cell wall made of cellulose, which provides structural support. This is a key feature that distinguishes them from animal cells.

distractorRationale.a: Plant cells contain chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
distractorRationale.c: Plant cells typically have a large central vacuole for storage.
distractorRationale.d: Plant cells usually have a single nucleus.

questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that break down waste materials and cellular debris. They are essential for recycling cellular components and maintaining cellular health.

distractorRationale.c: Vesicles transport materials but do not break down waste.

questions.explanation: The cell membrane is responsible for selective permeability, allowing certain substances to enter or exit the cell while preventing others. This is crucial for maintaining homeostasis.

distractorRationale.b: Ribosomes are involved in protein synthesis, not permeability.

questions.explanation: The nucleus is responsible for synthesizing ribosomal RNA (rRNA), which is a component of ribosomes. This is essential for protein synthesis.

distractorRationale.c: Cilia are involved in movement, not structural support.

It digests waste materials and cellular debris.
It provides energy for the cell.

questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes necessary for breaking down waste materials and cellular debris. They play a crucial role in maintaining the health of the cell by removing unwanted materials.

distractorRationale.b: Genetic information is stored in the nucleus, not in lysosomes.
